page_title: Bogart Marijuana Strain - Kind Green Buds

source_page_metadata.description: Explore the Bogart marijuana strain - THC levels, genetics, terpene profile, effects, flavor, and grow tips.

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Chemdawg 4 × SFV OG Kush
Breeder: Karma Genetics
THC Content: 20–26%
CBD Content: Low (<1%)
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , Myrcene , Limonene
Primary Flavors: Earthy, diesel, pine, herbal, spicy
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early to Mid-October
Indoor Yield: 400–550 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500–750 g/plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Some cannabis cultivars carry a certain gravitas the moment their aroma escapes the jar. Bogart belongs to that category—a strain whose bold diesel scent and heavy OG influence signal potency long before the first inhale. Named with a nod to classic cinematic swagger, the cultivar reflects the same kind of quiet authority: intense, unmistakable, and rooted in legendary genetics.

This indica-leaning hybrid emerged from the breeding work of Karma Genetics, a company respected for combining iconic cannabis lineages into refined modern cultivars. By blending the sharp chemical intensity of Chemdawg with the lemon-pine depth of SFV OG Kush, the breeder created a strain that captures the most recognizable traits of both parents.

For marijuana enthusiasts, the experience tends to revolve around physical relaxation paired with a calm, introspective mental state. The high unfolds with deliberate pacing—first easing the mind into a mellow headspace, then settling into a deeper body calm that feels particularly suited for late evening use. That balance between cerebral ease and muscular relaxation has helped the strain earn a steady following among cannabis connoisseurs who appreciate classic fuel-forward weed.
Genetics and Lineage

Bogart’s genetic blueprint comes from Karma Genetics, a breeding program known for emphasizing potency, terpene richness, and stable plant structure. The strain combines two powerful cannabis lineages: Chemdawg 4 and SFV OG Kush. Each parent brings a strong personality to the hybrid, creating a cultivar that reflects the defining traits of OG-family cannabis.

Chemdawg 4 represents one branch of the famous Chemdawg lineage, a family of strains that has profoundly influenced modern marijuana breeding . The original Chemdawg varieties became legendary for their sharp diesel aroma and powerful psychoactive effects. Many popular cannabis strains—including Sour Diesel and several OG Kush variants—trace part of their ancestry back to this genetic line. In Bogart, Chemdawg 4 contributes the pungent fuel-like terpene profile and robust resin production.

The second parent, San Fernando Valley OG Kush, introduces the citrus-heavy side of OG genetics. SFV OG is celebrated for its strong lemon-pine aroma and dense trichome coverage. Compared with some other OG phenotypes, it often produces a slightly brighter terpene profile, combining sharp citrus with classic earthy kush depth.

When these two genetic lines intersect, the resulting hybrid displays a fascinating combination of traits. Chemdawg brings raw pungency and potency, while SFV OG Kush contributes structure and citrus brightness. Together they create a cannabis strain that embodies the heavy fuel aroma and deeply relaxing effects that define many OG-dominant hybrids.
Effects and Experience

The experience with this cultivar usually begins with a subtle shift in mental tone. Rather than delivering an abrupt cerebral rush, the effects tend to creep in gradually. A gentle sense of euphoria emerges as the mind loosens its grip on daily worries. Thoughts slow slightly, creating a relaxed mental atmosphere that feels calm rather than foggy.

As the high deepens, the physical component begins to take center stage. Muscles loosen while a warm heaviness spreads through the limbs. This body effect can feel particularly soothing after long periods of activity or stress. Many marijuana enthusiasts describe the sensation as a gradual “unwinding” rather than an immediate couch-locking hit.

Later in the experience, the combination of mental calm and physical relaxation can encourage stillness and introspection. For some individuals, this phase promotes restful sleep. The duration of the effects often stretches several hours, reflecting the cultivar’s relatively high THC levels and dense terpene profile.
Medical Benefits

In medical cannabis circles, indica-dominant hybrids like Bogart are often associated with strong physical comfort. The relaxing body effect may help ease muscle tension that builds up from daily stress or physical exertion. Patients dealing with chronic discomfort sometimes seek out strains that combine physical relief with a manageable mental experience.

Stress and anxiety are also areas where this cultivar may offer support. The gradual calming of the mind can help quiet racing thoughts while promoting a sense of emotional steadiness. Unlike highly stimulating sativa strains , the mental effect here tends to feel grounded and soothing.

Sleep difficulties represent another reason some individuals gravitate toward heavier OG hybrids. As the high progresses into its later stages, the body relaxation can deepen into a tranquil, drowsy state. For those struggling to unwind at night, this progression may help encourage restful sleep.

In addition, the strain occasionally stimulates appetite during the later phases of the experience. For patients dealing with appetite loss due to medical treatments or chronic illness, cannabis strains that promote hunger can provide practical therapeutic benefits.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Opening a jar of Bogart immediately reveals a bold aromatic signature dominated by diesel fuel and sharp citrus. The scent feels unmistakably OG-driven, with lemon peel and pine weaving through the heavier chemical notes inherited from Chemdawg.

Breaking apart the dense buds intensifies the aromatic complexity. Earthy kush undertones emerge alongside subtle herbal spice. The terpene profile—typically rich in myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene—creates a layered fragrance that balances bright citrus with deep fuel pungency.

The flavor mirrors this complexity when smoked or vaporized. Initial inhales often deliver a sharp lemon-diesel taste that coats the palate with tangy citrus brightness. As the smoke settles, earthy pine and peppery spice become more noticeable, leaving behind a lingering kush aftertaste.

Visually, the flowers display many of the characteristics associated with OG-family marijuana strains . Dense olive-green buds are threaded with bright orange pistils and heavily coated with crystal trichomes. Under strong lighting, the resin layer can appear almost frosted, reflecting the plant’s excellent resin production.
Growing Information

Cultivating Bogart requires moderate experience but can reward attentive growers with aromatic, resin-rich flowers. The plant generally develops a sturdy structure typical of OG-dominant hybrids, producing thick branches capable of supporting dense buds during the flowering stage .

Indoor flowering typically takes around nine to ten weeks. As the plant approaches maturity, the aroma becomes increasingly pungent. Growers often rely on carbon filtration systems when cultivating indoors because the diesel scent can become extremely strong late in flowering.

Training techniques such as topping or low-stress training can improve canopy development. Encouraging lateral branching allows light to reach more bud sites, increasing overall yield potential. Proper airflow is also important because dense OG-style buds can trap moisture if humidity remains too high.

Outdoor cultivation performs best in warm, sunny climates with low humidity during late flowering. Under favorable conditions, the plant can produce respectable yields of sticky, terpene-rich buds. Harvest typically occurs in early autumn depending on the regional climate.
FAQ
Is Bogart an indica or sativa strain? The strain is considered an indica-dominant hybrid. Its effects lean strongly toward body relaxation and mental calm rather than energetic stimulation.

What does Bogart weed smell like? The aroma blends diesel fuel, lemon peel, earthy pine, and subtle herbal spice. These scents come from a terpene profile dominated by myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene.
How strong is Bogart marijuana? THC levels commonly range between 20% and 26%, placing it among the stronger cannabis strains found in many dispensaries.
Is Bogart good for nighttime use? Many users prefer consuming this cultivar during the evening because its relaxing body effects can encourage calmness and sleepiness.
How long does Bogart take to flower? Indoor flowering generally requires about nine to ten weeks, while outdoor plants are usually ready for harvest in early autumn.
Final Thoughts on Bogart

Bogart stands as a strong example of how carefully selected genetics can produce a cannabis strain with both potency and character. By combining Chemdawg 4 with SFV OG Kush, Karma Genetics created a hybrid that captures the unmistakable fuel-driven aroma and relaxing strength associated with classic OG family strains.

The cultivar appeals particularly to marijuana enthusiasts who appreciate pungent terpene profiles and deeply calming effects. Its flavor—layering citrus, pine, and diesel—offers the kind of sensory complexity that connoisseurs often seek in high-quality weed.

For growers, the plant delivers dense trichome-coated buds and a manageable cultivation experience when environmental conditions are properly controlled. Meanwhile, consumers benefit from a balanced high that begins with gentle euphoria before settling into full-body relaxation. In a cannabis landscape crowded with sweet fruit hybrids, Bogart remains proudly rooted in the bold fuel-and-kush tradition. Its genetics, aroma, and effects all reflect the enduring legacy of OG-style marijuana breeding.
